pages.text: Metal feet tap softly as Robo rolls forward. Gears, wires, and lights work together inside him.
People built Robo to help. Robots are machines made to do jobs carefully and safely.
Robo does not guess. He follows instructions one step at a time, just like a recipe.
Tiny sensors help Robo notice light, sound, or touch. Sensors are like robot senses.
When a box is in the way, Robo stops. Sensors send messages so he knows what is nearby.
Electric power keeps Robo moving. Batteries or plugs give robots the energy they need.
Robo can help clean floors, carry items, or build things in factories.
Even when Robo helps a lot, people stay in charge. Humans decide the rules and goals.
Robots do not feel hungry or tired. They work when powered and stop when turned off.
As lights dim, Robo powers down. Tomorrow, he will help again, step by careful step.
